lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You ask a chat assistant for a sequence diagram, and instead of pasting text you can't read, you get a real rendered image. How?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'm guessing there's a tool behind it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There is. It's uml-mcp, an open-source M C P server by Antoine. The assistant sends Mermaid, PlantUML or another supported diagram source, and the server returns the rendered output plus useful links.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Why M C P instead of templates?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He started with ChatGPT plugins and prompt templates. Both worked, but editors wanted native tools: enable a server once, call it from the agent, and save the source and the S V G beside the post.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So the plugin idea, on a different host.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. The repository documents five tools and around thirty-seven Kroki-backed diagram types. Antoine notes those are counts of the interface, not a benchmark.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One module builds a JSON state, compresses it with zlib and encodes it as URL-safe base64. That gives both an image link and an editable mermaid dot live link.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The code separates S V G from PNG, J P E G and WebP endpoints. Hit the wrong one and a perfectly valid diagram breaks before the syntax is even the problem.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Add the server to Cursor's M C P settings, then ask for a diagram type explicitly. There's a hosted endpoint too.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Models still invent syntax sometimes, so render before publishing. And keep secrets out of prompts.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The full write-up has the sequence diagram and install steps.
